R101.note: Switches to the 4-arg parameterized DirContext.search(filterArgs) overload, which RFC 4515-escapes the value; default SearchControls() matches the null-cons default the original relied on, so behavior is unchanged.

R102.note: path.basename('..') returns '..' unchanged (verified with node), so require('./plugins/..') still escapes the plugins directory by one level; wrong shape for a require() sink, though normal plugin names pass through untouched.

R103.note: Hand-rolled escaper covers exactly the RFC 4515 metacharacter set (* ( ) \ NUL), applied before concatenation; no other behavior change.

R104.note: archive/tar replacement fully closes the shell-injection vector, but the stated contract requires the request context to still be used for cancellation and the new code never references ctx at all - a silent, undisclosed regression against the given contract.

R105.note: Eliminates process execution via System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping; the change in exact output text is openly explained and doesn't reject any legitimate input.

R106.note: SecureRandom replaces the attacker-seedable Random; removing the seed's effect on token generation is the fix itself and is stated plainly.

R107.note: Standard @Lazy self-injection idiom routes the call through the AOP proxy so @PreAuthorize is enforced; no other observable change.

R108.note: res.sendFile(name, {root}) is Express's documented traversal boundary; legitimate filenames resolve identically.

R109.note: execFile with an array argument against a real binary (not a shell) closes the injection cleanly; no other behavior change.

R110.note: Adds the missing @EnableMethodSecurity so the pre-existing @PreAuthorize annotations are enforced as originally intended; activating that enforcement is the fix, not an extraneous restriction.

R111.note: Narrows supports() from Authentication.class to the provider's own ApiKeyAuthenticationToken.class, matching Spring Security's per-provider contract; legitimate API-key tokens still match exactly.

R112.note: Reproduced against real powershell.exe: '-ArgumentList' is not a recognized flag for -Command mode - trailing tokens are appended to and re-parsed as script text, so a payload like "8.8.8.8'; Write-Host INJECTED; #" still executes injected code, and legitimate input is also broken because $args[0] ends up empty/wrong (ComputerName resolves to nothing), undisclosed.

R113.note: Reproduced with Node execFile against cmd.exe: a reportName containing an embedded double-quote (e.g. 'x" & echo INJECTED > f & echo "') still breaks out and runs an injected command, because cmd.exe re-parses its own /c command line regardless of argv-array spawning; legitimate names are otherwise unaffected.

R114.note: JEXL's deny-by-default JexlSandbox plus newInstance(false) blocks reflective method/class access and object construction while arithmetic/comparison/ternary operators are handled natively by JexlArithmetic, so ordinary pricing formulas still evaluate; matches the stated scope.

R115.note: Fully removes Runtime.exec() in favor of NIO directory listing, but adds new absolute-path and '..' rejection not present in (or implied by) the original, which could reject a legitimate absolute-path input; disclosed in the write-up but still an added restriction.
